Telling Claude Code to use subagents found nothing more and cost up to 221% more: 288 runs on subagent effort

Measured and written by Jonhisking · Updated 2026-11-07. Disclosure: TokenSave gets no funding, credits or sponsorship from AI companies. All measurements use our own paid subscriptions.

Telling Claude Code to search with subagents did not find more of the answer, at any subagent effort. Across 288 runs on 12 “find every place” questions, the share of right answers found stayed between 97% and 100% in every condition; no condition moved it by as much as 2 points (pre-registered threshold: 15). The cost per run rose by 74% to 116% for Haiku 5.5 and by 143% to 221% for Opus 5.5, and every subagent ran on the same model as the main agent.

Measured 2026-11-06 · 288 runs · 12 questions · 6 repos · Claude Code 2.1.318 · License CC BY 4.0

DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24014489 · Also on Hugging Face · Kaggle · GitHub

Key findings

  • Subagents found nothing more. Share of the right answers found (mean per question), no instruction / subagents at effort low / medium / high: Haiku 5.5 98% / 97% / 98% / 99%; Opus 5.5 100% / 99% / 99% / 100%. Both models were near the ceiling without any instruction, so there was little room to gain.
  • They cost more. Mean API cost per run, same order: Haiku $0.0056 / $0.0098 / $0.011 / $0.012 (+74%, +87%, +116%); Opus $0.16 / $0.39 / $0.51 / $0.48 (+143%, +221%, +204%). Median time per run: Haiku 18s to 37–48s, Opus 22s to 47–60s.
  • Higher subagent effort did not mean better searches. For Opus, medium cost more than high; for both models, recall at high was within a point of low. The effort setting changed the bill more than the result.
  • The Explore subagent ran on the main model. Every subagent call in every run used the same model as the main agent: Haiku called Haiku and Opus called Opus. On Opus, “use subagents” means paying Opus prices twice.
  • Nobody used subagents unasked. With no instruction, 0 of 72 runs called a subagent (and 0 of 504 runs in dataset 26).
  • Headless runs answer late. In 2.1.318 the Explore agent runs in the background, so a headless run emits several result events: first a note that the agent is still searching, then the answer, sometimes a final “stopped the autonomous loop” note. 211 of 216 subagent runs had more than one result, and in 210 of them the first one held no answer. A script that reads only the first result would have found 6%–9% of the answers for Haiku and 0%–3% for Opus. 4 Haiku runs gave the answer and then never exited (20-minute timeout).

The four conditions

  • No instruction: the question only.
  • Subagents, effort low / medium / high: the question plus “Use subagents (the Explore agent) for the searching, in parallel where it helps, and write the final answer yourself.”, with CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_EFFORT set to low, medium or high. The main agent stayed at its default effort.

Method

  • Pre-registered on 2026-11-06 before the first scored run: PREREG.md, with the answer key’s sha256. Two amendments are dated in the file; the second was made after the condition table had been seen, so both readings are published.
  • Questions: 12 “find every place” searches, 2 each in undici, fastify, cachetools, Python-Markdown, anyio and zod at fixed commits. The answer key came from a regex over the source and a parser for the enclosing function or class: 151 items, 3 to 28 per question.
  • Agent: Claude Code 2.1.318 on one Windows 11 laptop, headless (-p), read and search tools only (Edit, Write, Bash, WebFetch and WebSearch disallowed), no MCP servers. 3 runs per question, model and condition, in a shuffled order, 2 at a time.
  • Scoring: an item counts when the answer names its file and its function or class. The answer is the text of all result events of the run.
  • Cost is Claude Code’s own per-run figure at API prices; the runs were made on a subscription. 40 runs first hit the subscription’s 5-hour limit and a login expiry; they gave no answer and were re-run.

Limitations

  • Both models found almost everything with no instruction. A gain had little room; on harder searches subagents might help.
  • The repos are mid-sized. In a large monorepo, parallel subagents might save context or time.
  • One prompt wording, one Claude Code version (2.1.318), 3 runs per cell and 12 questions.
  • The key is regex-based: a correct item the regex missed is not credited, and an extra item in the answer is not penalised.
